objective: Establish whether HolyAgent's pi extension can disable the T3 Code MCP tools it does not need when pi runs inside T3 Code, which ones those are, and how.
scope: Maintainer (verbatim): "t3code can delegate stuff with their mcp, can we disable whatever is unnecessary from it?". HolyAgent delegates through @tintinweb/pi-subagents, so T3's own delegation tools would duplicate it; T3's html_render, html_preview and preview_* tools are HolyAgent's visual route and stay.

Prior research: /home/user/holyagent-work/research/assignment-0mw6r54ng-kg9r.md (T3 injects an MCP bridge extension into pi under server key t3-code, exposing html_render, html_preview, preview_*, delegate_task, task_status, task_cancel, t3_thread_*, t3_pending_request).

Questions: (1) The full list of T3 tools a pi session gets, their exact names as pi sees them, and what each does; cite the T3 source (pingdotgg/t3code, PR #7211 and the orchestrator MCP server docs). (2) Whether a pi extension can remove or hide tools another extension registered: pi.setActiveTools / getActiveTools / getAllTools or similar in pi 1.5.0 (earendil-works/pi docs/extensions.md and types.ts), when it takes effect (session_start, before_agent_start), and whether it is stable across T3's session restarts and resume. (3) Whether T3 itself has a setting or launch option to turn off its delegation or thread tools for a provider, and whether any T3 tool is required for T3 to work (for example t3_pending_request for approvals or questions). (4) Effect on prompt caching: whether changing the active tool set mid-session changes the prompt prefix.
constraints: Authoritative sources first (T3 Code repository and docs, pi repository at 1.5.0 or main); label inference and third-party claims.
End with a table: tool, keep or disable, reason, and the mechanism, plus anything to verify later.

criteria.text: Tool list: names every T3 tool pi gets, with its purpose and source
Mechanism: states whether and how a pi extension can disable another extension's tools, with source
Recommendation: a keep or disable decision per tool with reasons, required tools identified
